name: Clementine
best_known_for: Joint BMDO + NASA lunar orbiter — first complete multispectral lunar map and the first evidence for water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters via bistatic radar
credit: Officially the Deep Space Program Science Experiment (DSPSE). Conceived by the Ballistic Missile Defense Organization (forerunner of the USSF Space Systems Command) to qualify lightweight sensors in deep-space conditions, with NASA collaborating on lunar + asteroid science. Launched 1994-01-25 on a Titan IIG from Vandenberg. Entered lunar polar orbit 1994-02-19 for 71 days of mapping; the multispectral imaging set covered every square kilometre of the Moon at 100-300 m resolution and 11 wavelengths — the first complete global lunar map. The bistatic radar experiment using Clementine's transmitter + DSN ground antennas found enhanced echoes at the south-pole Shackleton crater consistent with water ice, predating LCROSS by 15 years. A failed thruster firing after lunar departure aborted the planned asteroid Geographos flyby and ended the mission 1994-05.
